content: Acetaminophen and propoxyphene are medications that require careful use due to potential risks and side effects. Important Warning Propoxyphene, when taken in high doses, either alone or in combination with other drugs, has been linked to drug-related fatalities. It is critical not to take propoxyphene with other substances that cause drowsiness, such as alcohol, tranquilizers, sleep aids, antidepressants, or antihistamines. Additionally, do not exceed the prescribed dose, frequency, or duration of use as directed by your physician. Why This Medication is Prescribed This combination of acetaminophen and propoxyphene is prescribed to alleviate mild to moderate pain. It may also be used to reduce fever. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for further details. How This Medication Should Be Used The combination of acetaminophen and propoxyphene is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It is typically taken every four hours as needed. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take the medication exactly as directed. Propoxyphene has the potential to be habit-forming, so do not take larger doses, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer period than prescribed. Special Precautions Before taking acetaminophen and propoxyphene, inform your doctor and pharmacist if: You are allergic to acetaminophen, propoxyphene, sulfites, or any other medications. You are taking any prescription or nonprescription medications, especially acetaminophen (e.g., Tylenol), anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin), antidepressants, medications for cough, cold, or allergies, sedatives, seizure medications, sleeping pills, tranquilizers, or vitamins. You have or have had liver or kidney disease, a history of alcoholism, lung or thyroid disease, prostate enlargement, or urinary retention. You are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking this medication, contact your doctor immediately. You are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures. Inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking this medication. Be aware that this drug may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can enhance the drowsiness caused by this medication, so avoid consuming alcohol while taking it. What to Do If You Forget a Dose This medication is usually taken as needed. If your doctor has instructed you to take it regularly, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Side Effects Minor Side Effects Acetaminophen and propoxyphene may cause the following side effects. Notify your doctor if these symptoms are severe or persistent: Dizziness Lightheadedness Drowsiness Upset stomach Vomiting Constipation Stomach pain Rash Difficulty urinating Severe Side Effects If you experience any of the following symptoms, contact your doctor immediately: Difficulty breathing Mood changes If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor may report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Storage Conditions Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In Case of Emergency/Overdose In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911 immediately. Other Information Keep all appointments with your doctor. Excessive acetaminophen intake can cause liver damage; do not exceed 4000 mg of acetaminophen per day. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
